neuron-100m-bf16.note: One entry per NEFF SHAPE, which is the mini batch: a NEFF's leading dimension is FIXED, so every mini-batch size in the grid is a separate compile and a cell can only run a shape that exists. `source` is `compiled` when this lane built it and `s3-cache` when an earlier lane did -- a NEFF is a pure function of the seeded architecture, the target parameter count, the batch size AND the cast, so reusing one is reusing the same bytes, which the SHA-256 records. `load_proof_seconds` is a 20 s trickle of exactly `mini_batch` rows served by a FRESH server, so a NEFF that loads but cannot serve is found here rather than inside a cell's warm-up. `maximum_trace_error` is the compiled-versus-PyTorch error and is the PROOF of the cast: ~1e-6 at FP32, ~1e-2 once the matmuls are BF16, so the arms are distinguishable from this number alone.

metadata.auto_cast_default_note: neuronx-cc's own --auto-cast default is `matmult` on every release before SDK 2.28, so a compile that passes no flag produces BF16 matrix multiplies. Both arms of this campaign pass the flag explicitly; a NEFF whose metadata has no `auto_cast` key was built before this was understood and its `precision` field cannot be trusted.
metadata.compile_route_note: torch_neuronx.trace compiles the parameters in as CONSTANTS, so the NEFF takes one input -- the [batch, width] feature tensor -- which is the contract hushar's backend serves. The torch-neuronx 2.14 dynamo backend was evaluated and cannot replace it: it writes no model NEFF to disk, and the graph it lowers is stateless, so a NEFF built from its StableHLO takes weights as inputs and hushar refuses it. Same route as config-sweep-neuron-trn1-10M-50M.
metadata.precision_note: --auto-cast=matmult --auto-cast-type=bf16, so the matrix-multiply engine runs in BF16 and normalization and accumulation stay FP32 -- the same division TensorRT's --bf16 makes on the GPU
